title: Kilian Ort to replace Danny Heister as Borussia Düsseldorf head coach after 17 years
seo_title: Kilian Ort to succeed Danny Heister at Borussia Düsseldorf
description: Borussia Düsseldorf have named Kilian Ort, 30, as head coach from 2027-28 on a two-year deal, ending Danny Heister's 17 years in charge of the Bundesliga club.
standfirst: The 30-year-old, who retired as a player last year and now coaches Bundesliga rivals ASC Grünwettersbach, takes over in the summer on a two-year contract.
body: Borussia Düsseldorf have appointed Kilian Ort as their head coach from the 2027-28 season, ending Danny Heister's 17 years in charge of the Bundesliga leaders.

Ort, 30, has signed a two-year contract and will take over in the summer. The announcement came a day after his current team, ASC Grünwettersbach, lost 3-0 to Düsseldorf in the Tischtennis Bundesliga, the match in which [Fan Zhendong returned](/news/fan-zhendong-borussia-dusseldorf-return-unbeaten-bundesliga-2026.html) after seven weeks out.

Ort stopped playing less than two years ago. A former Germany international from Neustadt an der Saale, he reached 48th in the world rankings, was runner-up at the German Championships in 2018 and played his Bundesliga table tennis for TSV Bad Königshofen. Chronic disc problems in his back forced him to stop playing early in 2025, aged 28.

He became Grünwettersbach's coach in September 2025. The Karlsruhe club are bottom of the Bundesliga with two wins from eight matches, and Ort said his attention would stay on them until the season ends. "I want to finish the season with Grünwettersbach as successfully as possible," he said (translated from German).

Of the Düsseldorf job, he said: "I consider it a great honour that the club leadership trusts me with the role of head coach of Borussia Düsseldorf. It will be a monumental task for me to step into the big footsteps of Danny Heister," he said (translated from German), adding that he felt ready for the challenge.

Heister, from the Netherlands, has won more than 20 titles with Düsseldorf. The club gave no reason for the change beyond a decision that it was time for something new. "With Danny we worked together for 17 wonderful and very successful years. We have now decided that it is time to go new ways," said Andreas Preuß, the club's manager (translated from German). He described Ort as an ambitious German head coach who would bring fresh ideas while building on what the club had achieved.

Heister has one more season, and he wants it to end with a trophy. "Borussia and I still have a shared task," he said. "We want to win at least one more title together" (translated from German). "I wish Kilian much success in the big task that follows."

The timing suits a club in form. Düsseldorf have won all eight of their league matches this season and lead the Bundesliga with 16 points, four clear of 1. FC Saarbrücken and TTF Ochsenhausen. Fan, signed in July, is unbeaten in eight league singles, and Anton Källberg, Kanak Jha and Dang Qiu make up the rest of a strong squad. They also beat AS Pontoise-Cergy 3-1 in the first leg of their [ETTU Champions League last-16 tie](/news/ettu-champions-league-men-2026-27-last-16-pontoise-dusseldorf.html) last week.

Preuß said this month that no player or coach at the club has a contract beyond this season, so Ort's appointment is the first decision about next year. Talks with Fan and the rest of the squad are still to come ([more on the contract talks](/news/borussia-dusseldorf-fan-zhendong-contracts-2026.html)).

Heister's next match in charge is the league's top game, against Saarbrücken in Trier on Sunday 22 November at 2.30pm UK time. Düsseldorf host Pontoise-Cergy in the Champions League return leg on 18 December.
